findings.description: その子、増長するから程々になさいよ becomes This kid is getting arrogant, so calm her down, replacing advice to moderate playing along with a direct calming instruction.

contexts.japanese:
「……ベアトって付き合いがいいのね。
その子、増長するから程々になさいよ。
じゃあね、私は席を外すわ」
contexts.japanesePC: 「……ベアトって付き合いがいいのね。その子、増長するから程々になさいよ。じゃあね、私は席を外すわ。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「……ベアトって付き合いがいいのね。
その子、増長するから程々になさいよ。
じゃあね、私は席を外すわ」
contexts.WH: "......Nice job playing along with her, Beato.  This kid's getting arrogant, so calm her down.  See you, I'm leaving."
contexts.MG:
"...You're a real good sport, Beato.
This kid tends to get full of herself, so try not to overdo it.
See you, I'm leaving."
contexts.UP:
"......You're good at playing along with her, Beato.
This kid can get a little full of herself, so don't take it too far.
See you, I'm leaving."
contexts.note: Both restore moderating Beato’s playing along.

findings.sourceReading: Bern comments that Beatrice is accommodating, then advises her not to indulge Lambda too much because it will make Lambda conceited.
findings.alternative: Both discourage encouraging Lambda, but English asserts present arrogance and asks Beatrice to act on Lambda rather than limit her own indulgence.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: 次のゲームの準備が整ったら呼ぼうぞ becomes I shall call for some after preparing for the next game.

contexts.japanese:
「そうか、わかったぞ。
試してみよう。
次のゲームの準備が整ったら呼ぼうぞ。
それまでゆっくり戦略でも練るが良い」
contexts.japanesePC: 「そうか、わかったぞ。試してみよう。次のゲームの準備が整ったら呼ぼうぞ。それまでゆっくり戦略でも練るが良い。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「そうか、わかったぞ。
試してみよう。
次のゲームの準備が整ったら呼ぼうぞ。
それまでゆっくり戦略でも練るが良い」
contexts.WH: "Oh, I see.  I shall try it.  I shall call for some after preparing for the next game.  Until then, feel free to polish up your strategy at your leisure."
contexts.MG:
"Oh, I see.
I shall try it.
I'll call for some after preparing the next game.
Until then, feel free to polish up your strategy at your leisure."
contexts.UP:
"I see. Alright.
I shall try it.
I shall call for you when the preparations are finished for the next game.
Until then, feel free to draw up a strategy at your leisure."
contexts.note: MG calls for some, retaining the misplaced supplies referent; UP restores calling Bernkastel.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice agrees to try the tea suggestion, then promises to call Bernkastel when the next game is ready and tells her to devise strategy until then.
findings.alternative: The immediately preceding gochujang suggestion could explain some in English, but the next-game readiness and waiting strategy mark a summons to Bern rather than ordering condiment.

findings.description: ベルンカステルを煙に撒く becomes speaking in riddles for Bernkastel's sake.

contexts.japanese:
私が聞きたいくらいよ。
………あんたのゲームには、遊びが多い。
…それは時にベルンカステルを煙に巻くから、あんたなりの策略なんだと、私も最初は思ってた」
contexts.japanesePC: 「どういう意味？　私が聞きたいくらいよ。………あんたのゲームには、遊びが多い。…それは時にベルンカステルを煙に撒くから、あんたなりの策略なんだと、私も最初は思ってた。
contexts.japanesePS3:
私が聞きたいくらいよ。
………あんたのゲームには、遊びが多い。
…それは時にベルンカステルを煙に巻くから、あんたなりの策略なんだと、私も最初は思ってた」
contexts.WH: "What do I mean?  That's what I want to hear.  .........You play a lot in your game.  ...At first, I thought you were speaking in riddles for Bernkastel's sake every now and then, as part of your tactics.
contexts.MG:
That's what I want to hear.
......You play around a lot in your game.
...Sometimes, that ends up confusing Bernkastel, so at first I thought it was some special strategy of yours."
contexts.UP:
That's what I want to ask you.
.........You play around a lot in your games.
...At first, I thought it was part of your tactics, because it would completely baffle Bernkastel from time to time."
contexts.note: Both restore confounding Bernkastel rather than speaking for her sake.

findings.sourceReading: Lambda initially thought Beatrice's playful flourishes were strategy because they sometimes bewildered or threw Bernkastel off.
findings.alternative: Speaking in riddles can bewilder someone, but for her sake introduces a beneficiary rather than the target of obfuscation, and source describes an effect rather than specifically riddling speech.

findings.description: あんたはゲーム盤である必要なんかない becomes There is no need for this to be a game board for you.

contexts.japanese:
「……………だからアンタは使えないのよ。
あんたはゲーム盤である必要なんかない。
ベルンカステルを、永遠にここに閉じ込める鳥篭でさえあればいいの」
contexts.japanesePC: 「……………だからアンタは使えないのよ。あんたはゲーム盤である必要なんかない。ベルンカステルを、永遠にここに閉じ込める鳥篭でさえあればいいの。
contexts.japanesePS3:
「……………だからアンタは使えないのよ。
あんたはゲーム盤である必要なんかない。
ベルンカステルを、永遠にここに閉じ込める鳥篭でさえあればいいの」
contexts.WH: "..................This is why you're useless.  There's no need for this to be a game board for you.  It's alright if this is a bird cage to lock Bernkastel up here for all eternity.
contexts.MG:
".........This is why you're useless.
There's no need for you to be a game board.
You just have to be a bird cage that can lock Bernkastel up here for all eternity."
contexts.UP:
"...............This is why you're useless.
There's no need for this to be a game board for you.
It simply needs to be a bird cage to lock Bernkastel up here for all eternity."
contexts.note: MG restores Beato as board or cage; UP retains this being a board for you.

findings.sourceReading: Lambda tells Beatrice that she need not be a game board, only a birdcage imprisoning Bernkastel forever.
findings.alternative: The board is Beatrice's instrument and both versions retain cage imagery, but source directly equates Beatrice with the demanded function; English switches to an external this with Beatrice as beneficiary/user.

findings.description: WH changes Lambda’s condition for continued sponsorship from trying to remain the certain victor to repeatedly trying to become the victor.

contexts.japanese: ……あなたが“絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする限り、私は絶対の魔女として、あなたに力を与えるわ。
contexts.japanesePC: 「いいこと？　あんたの役目は、ベルンカステルを屈服させることよ。つまりゲームに、永遠に勝者でいること。……あなたが“絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする限り、私は絶対の魔女として、あなたに力を与えるわ。…………でも。
contexts.japanesePS3: ……あなたが“絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする限り、私は絶対の魔女として、あなたに力を与えるわ。
contexts.WH: "You know what?  Your role is to make Bernkastel surrender.  In other words, that means being the victor in this game for all eternity.  ......As long as you keep trying to become the 'certain' victor, then I will give you my power as the Witch of Certainty.  ............However.
contexts.MG: ...As long as you keep trying to become the victor "with certainty", then I'll give you my power as the Witch of Certainty.
contexts.UP: ......As long as you keep trying to become the certain victor, then I will give you my power as the Witch of Certainty.
contexts.note: The preceding eternal-victory sentence makes the intended requirement recoverable, and keep trying carries persistence, but become describes attaining the position rather than retaining it.

findings.sourceReading: “絶対”の勝者であり続けようとする requires Beato to seek to continue being the certain victor, maintaining unbroken victory.
findings.alternative: The preceding eternal-victory sentence makes the intended requirement recoverable, and keep trying carries persistence, but become describes attaining the position rather than retaining it.

findings.description: WH transfers the restriction from where Bernkastel can sing or cry to what she can do, saying she can do nothing except cry in Lambda’s palm.

contexts.japanese: …私の手の平でしか鳴けないように、たっぷりと仕込んであげるんだから」
contexts.japanesePC: ……そしてあなたが屈服したら、…私の手の平でしか鳴けないように、たっぷりと仕込んであげるんだから。
contexts.japanesePS3: …私の手の平でしか鳴けないように、たっぷりと仕込んであげるんだから」
contexts.WH: ......And when you surrender, ...I'll train you so that you can't do anything other than cry in the palm of my hand.
contexts.MG: ...I'll train you so that you can't do anything other than cry in the palm of my hand."
contexts.UP: ...I'll train you so that you can't tweet in anyone's palm but mine."
contexts.note: Both imply coercive captivity, but inability to do anything except cry is a stronger and differently scoped limitation than exclusive dependence on the specified place or person.

findings.sourceReading: 私の手の平でしか鳴けない means she will be trained so she can sing or cry only in Lambda’s palm, continuing the captive-bird metaphor.
findings.alternative: Both imply coercive captivity, but inability to do anything except cry is a stronger and differently scoped limitation than exclusive dependence on the specified place or person.

contexts.japanese: 「何よ何よ、何で私にだけ教えてくれないのよ、意地悪ぅー！！
contexts.japanesePS3: 「何よ何よ、何で私にだけ教えてくれないのよ、意地悪ぅー！！
contexts.MG: "Come on, come on, why won't you tell only me, you meanie?!!
contexts.UP: "Why, why, why I am the only one you won't tell, you meanie!!

findings.sourceReading: Lambda asks why she alone is not told.
findings.alternative: The meaning is clear but subject–auxiliary inversion is required. PCWH210630 and MG are grammatical.
